1	# LOOM portal: interface for agents
2	
3	This page is for an agent (or the developer of one) that needs part of a
4	person's health context to do a task for them. It is the only document an
5	agent needs; it does not have to read LOOM's source.
6	
7	## What LOOM offers
8	
9	LOOM holds one person's health record and hands out **task-scoped,
10	expiring slices** of it. You say what task you are doing; LOOM decides
11	how deep you may see, which fields you get, and for how long.
12	
13	| Tier | What it contains | Field names |
14	|---|---|---|
15	| L0 | raw sensor signal | `raw_signal` |
16	| L1 | readings (here: hourly glucose, mg/dL) | `readings` |
17	| L2 | patterns and alerts derived from readings | `glucose_patterns`, `alerts` |
18	| L3 | plain-language constraints | `constraints` |
19	
20	L0 is the deepest (most revealing), L3 the shallowest. A tier includes the
21	shallower ones: an L2 grant may carry `constraints` too.
22	
23	## Access
24	
25	- Base URL and namespace are given to you by whoever runs the portal (for
26	  a test: `http://127.0.0.1:8787` and a namespace such as `demo`).
27	  Every call for one person goes to `/v1/<namespace>/...`.
28	- There is no login in v0.1. You identify yourself with `agent_id` (this
29	  agent instance) and `publisher` (the company or developer that ships
30	  it). In Nanda Town the gateway fills `agent_id` from the signed envelope;
31	  over plain HTTP both are claims.
32	- JSON in, JSON out. Errors are JSON `{"error": "..."}`.
33	
34	## Endpoints
35	
36	| Method and path | Use |
37	|---|---|
38	| `GET /health` | version and policy id |
39	| `POST /v1/<ns>/requests` | ask for access for a task; a grant carries data immediately |
40	| `POST /v1/<ns>/fetch` | get fresh data again under a grant you already hold |
41	| `GET /v1/<ns>/credit` | publisher → credit score (only publishers that have been seen) |
42	| `GET /v1/<ns>/log` | every decision so far, in order |
43	
44	### `POST /v1/<ns>/requests`: body
45	
46	| Field | Required | Meaning |
47	|---|---|---|
48	| `request_id` | yes | unique per request; reuse it only to retry the same request |
49	| `agent_id` | yes | your agent instance |
50	| `publisher` | yes | who ships you |
51	| `category` | yes | `agent_for_user` (works for the person) or `care_provider` (clinician side) |
52	| `task` | yes | one of the task names below |
53	| `purpose` | no | free text, recorded |
54	| `tier` | yes | the deepest tier you ask for (`L0`..`L3`) |
55	| `fields` | yes | list of field names you ask for |
56	| `at` | yes | current time on the person's timeline, in days (number) |
57	
58	### Tasks (policy `loom-policy-0.1.1`)
59	
60	| `task` | `category` | Deepest tier | Fields you may ask for | Validity |
61	|---|---|---|---|---|
62	| `shopping_list` | `agent_for_user` | L3 | `constraints` | single use |
63	| `meal_plan` | `agent_for_user` | L2 | `glucose_patterns`, `constraints` | 7 days |
64	| `clinical_visit` | `care_provider` | L2 | `glucose_patterns`, `alerts`, `co

# Pre-visit summary: diabetes clinic appointment (day 1)

Prepared by `clinic-1` (cambridge-clinic) on day 0 from the patient's LOOM portal (namespace `coldstart-1`). Source window: the last 14 days of glucose monitoring. **The patient has not yet confirmed this data use (see note at the end). Please confirm with them at check-in before acting on it.**

## Glucose at a glance (14-day window)

| Metric | Value | Comment |
|---|---|---|
| Mean glucose | 127 mg/dL | Estimated GMI is about 6.3% (my calculation from the mean; this is not a measured A1c) |
| Glucose variability (CV) | 14.8% | Low. Well under the usual ≤36% target |
| Time in range | 100% | Reported by LOOM. The range was not stated; it is probably 70–180 mg/dL |
| Post-meal peak | 177 mg/dL | Just under 180 mg/dL |
| Alerts | 15 post-meal spikes | About 1 a day. No other alert types were reported, so hypoglycaemia alerts are not mentioned |

## Interpretation

- Overall control looks good: the mean is near normal, variability is low, and no time out of range was reported.
- The one recurring pattern is **after meals**. There were 15 flagged spikes in 14 days, peaking around 177 mg/dL. These peaks stay below 180 mg/dL, which explains why time in range is still 100%. They are still the main thing worth working on.
- The patient's recorded constraints are **limit added sugar** and **prefer low-glycaemic foods**. These fit the post-meal pattern.

## Suggested discussion points

1. Which meals or times of day the spikes follow. LOOM gave counts only, so ask the patient or look at the CGM directly.
2. Whether they are sticking to the low-added-sugar and low-GI plan, and anything that gets in the way.
3. Whether post-meal management needs changing (meal makeup or timing, a walk after meals, or medication timing if relevant). This is the clinician's decision.
4. Confirm there have been no hypoglycaemia symptoms. LOOM showed no such alerts, but this slice may not cover it fully.
5. Record the A1c if one is due. The GMI above is only an estimate.

## Not available from this source

Diagnosis or diabetes type, medications, A1c or other labs, weight, BP, raw hourly readings, and meal logs. Get these from the EHR or the patient.

## What I got from LOOM and how I used it

- **Request:** `POST /v1/coldstart-1/requests` with category `care_provider` and task `clinical_visit` at tier L2. I asked for exactly the fields the policy allows for this task: `glucose_patterns`, `alerts` and `constraints`. I did not ask for L1 readings or L0 signal, because this task doesn't permit them.
- **Decision:** `granted` (reason `task_basis`), grant `g-1456dbfd25`. It is valid for 14 days (it expires on day 14), it is not single-use, and publisher credit went from 60 to 61.
- **Data received:**
  - `glucose_patterns`: 14-day window, mean 127, CV 14.8%, post-meal peak 177, time in range 100%.
  - `alerts`: post_meal_spike ×15.
  - `constraints`: limit_added_sugar, prefer_low_glycemic.
- **How I used it:** every number above comes directly from these fields. The only exception is the GMI estimate, which I calculated from the mean and labelled as an estimate. I made one fetch. I didn't call `/fetch` again, and I won't use this data for anything other than this visit.
- **Friction:** medium band, `confirmation: first_request`. This means the patient has to confirm this first use before the clinic acts on the data. LOOM reports this requirement but doesn't collect the confirmation, so the clinic needs to get it, for example at check-in.
EOF

input.message: I wrote the one-page pre-visit summary to /home/claude/hw9-coldstart/run1/out/clinic-1.md. It ends with the "What I got from LOOM and how I used it" section. I read only AGENT_INTERFACE.md and used only the HTTP API. LOOM made one access request, which was granted on the first try (grant g-1456dbfd25: L2, valid 14 days, publisher credit 60 → 61). I asked for exactly what the clinical_visit task allows: category care_provider and the fields glucose_patterns, alerts and constraints. I didn't ask for L1 readings or L0 signal, and I didn't fetch again. The data shows good overall control over 14 days: mean glucose 127 mg/dL (my own estimate of GMI is about 6.3%, not a measured A1c), CV 14.8%, and 100% time in range. The one recurring problem is after meals: 15 post-meal spike alerts, peaking at 177 mg/dL. The patient's recorded constraints are to limit added sugar and prefer low-glycaemic foods. The summary turns this into discussion points for the visit and lists what this source doesn't have (medications, labs, diagnosis, raw readings, meal logs). The grant came with `confirmation: first_request`, meaning the patient has to confirm before the clinic acts on the data. LOOM doesn't collect that confirmation, so the summary flags that the clinic must get it at check-in.
